authorResearch.method: Every catalogue name compared locally against the complete retrieved Wikidata authority subset (human, historical scientific, technical, medical, and scholarly occupations, born before 1950). Exact normalized names, given names, initials, and constrained OCR spelling hypotheses; homonyms retained separately. This is not an exhaustive search of every public authority.
authorResearch.sourceMetadata: Wikidata CC0; Wikimedia images retain their individual licenses linked on credit pages.
authorResearch.scoreMeaning: Heuristic match ranking, not a calibrated probability.

methodology.approach: All catalogue records searched locally against public Internet Archive metadata. Token-index retrieval followed by fuzzy title, creator and publication-year scoring. Two distinct best metadata candidates retained. This is candidate generation, not a verified catalogue crosswalk.
methodology.confidence: Heuristic tiers, not calibrated probabilities. High requires close title, creator overlap and same/adjacent year; medium supports a plausible work connection; low can be an OCR, translation, edition or false-match lead.
methodology.imagePolicy: Source thumbnails are reference-copy images. Page type and edition match unverified unless separately researched. No image inferred to depict the family copy.
methodology.copyCountPolicy: External record, digitization and search-result counts are never converted into surviving physical copies.
methodology.scope: Scientific and historical collections plus science-related subject records dated through 1965, selected through the query saved in book-cache/ia-corpus-log.json. Every one of the 49,780 family catalogue records was attempted; a no-candidate classification means the selected corpus did not produce a sufficiently plausible match, not that the book lacks other records worldwide.

survivalHighlights.title: Essay d’analyse sur les jeux de hazard
survivalHighlights.summary: Four distinct institutional copies are documented: Valenciennes, BnF, IFoA and Ghent. This is a located minimum for the 1708 edition across issues. No worldwide census, reliable upper bound or survival rate was found. Auction appearances were excluded because a copy can be sold repeatedly.

survivalHighlights.title: Essay d’analyse sur les jeux de hazard · second edition
survivalHighlights.summary: Three independent institutional copies are located at IFoA, the Edward Worth Library and the Russian State Library. RSL’s microfilm entry is not an additional physical copy; IFoA’s modern facsimile is excluded. No worldwide upper bound or defensible point estimate was found.

survivalHighlights.title: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas maximi minimive proprietate gaudentes
survivalHighlights.summary: Two independent institutional copies: Smithsonian and Carnegie Mellon’s Posner Collection. The Internet Archive mirror of the Smithsonian scan counts once. Repeated sale descriptions in the Posner dossier are not additional copies. The worldwide total remains unestimated.

survivalHighlights.title: Sage · Moyens de remédier aux poisons · 1811
survivalHighlights.summary: The author reports 500 first-edition copies printed. One institutional copy is documented here. Conditional bounds: 1–500, low confidence for survival; this is not a likely surviving range.

survivalHighlights.title: Philosophiae naturalis principia mathematica · 1714
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 4 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. At least four distinct institutional copies are documented. Jorink and Zuidervaart estimate an original print run of about 750 for this Amsterdam edition, inferred from ten publishers receiving the same 75-copy share as in the later venture. This is a printing estimate, not a count of surviving copies. A conditional ceiling near 750 is useful context, but a likely surviving range is not established; the 1687 census does not apply.

survivalHighlights.title: Philosophiae naturalis principia mathematica, editio altera with Le Seur and Jacquier commentary · 1760
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 2 documented complete three-volume sets. Two complete three-volume sets of the 1760 printing are documented. Three physical volumes constitute one set. Wellcome currently exposes two volumes online but explicitly catalogues a complete physical set. The family OCR matches the Philibert imprint and edition statement. No reliable worldwide census or original print run was established.

survivalHighlights.title: Tractatus sive physiologia nova de magnete · 1628
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 86 documented known copies of the 1628 edition across title-page states. The 2026 published census reports 86 known copies of the 1628 Stettin edition across its title-page states. This count does not describe only the Hallervord issue named on the family card. The 2025 analytical snapshot contains 77 entries for this edition; it is an earlier dataset/subset, not 77 additional copies. Undiscovered copies and a finite worldwide upper bound are not established.

survivalHighlights.title: Libri quinque de mensuris et ponderibus · 1533
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 56 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. The BnF bibliography reports at least 56 copies at 50 listed institutions/departments. This total includes imperfect copies (one Mazarine copy lacks its title). It is a count of reported holdings, not a complete worldwide census. No survival-rate extrapolation is justified. The Paris printing follows the Basel printing of the same year; they must not be combined.

survivalHighlights.title: Historia naturalis · 1499
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 11 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. A holding library reports six Hungarian copies; five additional named holdings outside Hungary give a conservative documentary lower bound of 11. This is not a count of the full ISTC record, which was not retrievable in this research pass. The family card says 264 leaves while external descriptions commonly give 268; completeness of the family copy needs inspection.

survivalHighlights.title: Elementorum libri XV, with Proclus’s commentary · 1533
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 5 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. Five physical copies are explicitly reported by four holding institutions. The 1533 Greek text must be distinguished from the 1537 and 1558 Latin printings. The Latin and Greek texts bound together at Princeton do not make two copies of the 1533 edition.

survivalHighlights.title: Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze · 1655
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 4 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. Four institutional copies of the 1655 printing are documented. Some copies are bound within the collected Opere; those constituent texts are counted once each, not as additional complete sets. No census or print run for this printing was established.

survivalHighlights.title: Bermannus sive de re metallica · 1530
survivalHighlights.summary: At least 1 documented physical copies, including imperfect copies unless otherwise stated. One fully identified institutional reference copy is documented here. This short dialogue is Agricola’s Bermannus, not the later twelve-book De re metallica first published in 1556. Descriptions of that later work’s woodcuts and circulation must not be carried over.

sourceVerification.definition: A verified match has a manually researched edition comparison, high metadata confidence, and a cited external source. Automated candidates, medium-confidence edition matches, images alone, and author biographies do not qualify. This verifies the bibliographic connection, not the physical family copy.

crossrefRetrieval.scope: Bounded historical article corpus. Up to 8000 metadata records per selected journal dated1600–1965, in API default order. Not individual searches for every family record.

coverageSummary.validation: PASS: complete record coverage, distinct relationship types, no automatic verified flags, no scan-to-survivor conversions, and complete image/source provenance fields.

matchingMethod.approach: All catalogue records screened locally against public Internet Archive and a bounded Crossref journal-article metadata corpus. OCR f/£ repair, line-break repair, shortened imprint-free title variants, phonetic token normalization and near-spelling retrieval precede fuzzy title, creator and publication-year scoring. Two distinct best metadata candidates retained. This is candidate generation, not a verified catalogue crosswalk.
matchingMethod.confidence: Heuristic tiers, not calibrated probabilities. High requires close title, creator overlap and same/adjacent year; medium supports a plausible work connection; low can be an OCR, translation, edition or false-match lead.
matchingMethod.imagePolicy: Source thumbnails are reference-copy images. Page type and edition match unverified unless separately researched. No image inferred to depict the family copy.
matchingMethod.copyCountPolicy: External record, digitization and search-result counts are never converted into surviving physical copies.
matchingMethod.scope: All family catalogue records were screened locally, not individually searched on the web. Internet Archive corpus source selection is recorded in the earlier broad-research/book-cache/ia-corpus-log.json. The added bounded Crossref journal corpus and its requests are recorded in full-catalogue-pass/cache/crossref-retrieval-log.json. Unmatched records may be absent from these corpora, have unreadable OCR, or need other sources; this is not an exhaustive search of world catalogues.
matchingMethod.containerPolicy: Host-publication candidates are inferred from an OCR offprint citation. They identify a possible reading source, not the article, edition, physical offprint or survival count. No individual external request was sent for these records; matching uses the cached Internet Archive corpus.
matchingMethod.externalSearchScope: One family title was individually probed through Crossref and OpenAlex. All 49,780 family records were locally screened; the main external activity was public-corpus retrieval (93 Crossref batch requests plus journal discovery), not 49,780 web searches.
matchingMethod.reviewedFalsePositiveProtections: Spot-checking exposed publisher/imprint words matching unrelated book reviews. Three named regression records were rechecked after removing imprint variants: Das Gold and Mathematische Schwingungslehre no longer matched unrelated reviews; Molecular rays now matched a source with that title. Common publication-format tokens are excluded. Low-confidence related-title mismatches still remain and are explicitly labelled.
matchingMethod.falsePositivePolicy: Low-confidence candidates can be false matches. Imprints and common publication-format words are removed before title matching; apparent book reviews and host-journal leads are separately labelled. No automatic candidate is marked verified.

fullCataloguePass.publicationConfidencePolicy: Automatic candidate confidence is capped at medium on the site. High similarity scores do not establish an individually verified edition.

catalogueMethod.title: Original-catalogue evidence screening
catalogueMethod.universe: All 49,780 records from the original OCR text, matched to their original PDF filename and one-based scan page.
process: Scan all records for scarcity words, edition limitation/numbering, manuscripts, reproduction/printing notes, offprints and incompleteness.
Read all 93 scarcity,95 printing,122 manuscript,29 reproduction and 134 incompleteness candidate contexts. Reject title words and subject terminology.
Visually inspect the four numerical printing notes in the original PDF scans. Inspect the preceding Torricelli card to connect the continuation correctly.
Use automatic OCR matches for explicit abbreviated offprint notation and typescript/duplicated-copy notes; expose the short original context and retain medium/lowconfidence.
Review manuscript-catalogue headings and group continuation cards with the first card. Detect explicit cross-reference/continuation markers, including ones missing from the old flags.
Retain all 49,780 IDs in a compact assessment index, including records where no explicit signal was found.
scope: This is a catalogue evidence pass, not an external institutional search for every edition.
No original publication date or age alone is used to assign rarity.
No signal found means no explicit evidence detected by this method; it does not mean non-rare or absent from other libraries.
An offprint marker can describe a journal extract or clipping; a separately printed offprint has not been proved.
Manuscript objects can be individually distinctive while the same text exists in other manuscripts or print. No global count is assigned.
A facsimile may itself be limited; its print run belongs to that reproduction, not the earlier original.
Numbered copies do not prove a total without a limitation statement.
Original print-run numbers give only conditional ceilings, never present-day survivor estimates.
Completeness, presentation inscriptions and handwritten additions are copy-specific attributes, not global edition rarity.
Cross-references and continuation cards are not independently counted as books; manuscript continuations and Torricelli are explicitly linked. Other records remain undeduplicated catalogue records.
